lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
Date of birth: 2 Nov 1996 | Nationality: American
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Measured the onboarding redesign by comparing merchants who opted into the new flow with those who stayed on the old one.
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Mar 2019 - Aug 2023
- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Coordinated the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations and prepares the forecast pack for each meeting.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Held weekly working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling across the network.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Halved the time it takes a new merchant to receive a first payment, across 2,300 merchants, by redesigning onboarding.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Use the full professional LinkedIn URL if possible.
Confirm that the LinkedIn profile is complete and consistent with the resume.
Remove the date of birth.
items.because: It is not relevant to your qualifications and can create avoidable age-bias concerns.

items.says: Remove the nationality unless a specific application requires it.
items.because: It is only needed for some work-authorization or government-compliance requirements.

items.says: Clarify whether the MBA is completed or in progress.
items.because: The dates end in June 2025, so the status should match your actual situation.

items.says: Consider adding only relevant GPA, honors, coursework, leadership, or major-project details if they are strong.
Add a concentration, honors, or relevant analytical coursework if it supports the targeted roles.
Define whether the 35% increase is relative or percentage-point.
State the measurement period for the conversion increase.
State the size of the merchant or customer population measured.
Explain whether the result came from an A/B test, before-and-after comparison, or another method.
Clarify the scope of “for all merchants.”
items.because: It sounds unusually broad and may invite questions about rollout scope and causality.

items.says: Distinguish your contribution from the result of the entire product or engineering team.
Clarify whether the dispute self-service product actually launched.
Add a measurable post-launch outcome such as support volume, resolution time, or dispute completion.
items.because: Those effects would be more valuable than schedule performance alone.

items.says: Clarify whether you owned the planning, coordination, or delivery process that affected the early shipment.
Use a consistent currency format instead of spelling out the amount.
Clarify whether $1.1 million represents total losses, preventable losses, or an estimate.
Explain how the interviews and six months of data produced an annual estimate.
items.because: Readers may question how those inputs led to the annual figure.

items.says: Specify whether the roadmap priority was approved, funded, or actually delivered.
Use a spelling convention consistent with the U.S.-oriented resume rather than switching to “analysed.”
Clarify whether you personally closed the tickets or coordinated their resolution.
Explain the significance of closing 140 tickets through resolution time, backlog age, or merchant impact.
items.because: “Closing” could mean administrative closure rather than solving user problems.

items.says: Define the comparison period for cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
Add the result of the onboarding measurement and what you learned or changed.
items.because: The bullet currently describes an evaluation method but not its result.

items.says: Address possible selection bias in comparing merchants who opted in with those who did not.
items.because: The two groups may differ systematically.

items.says: Connect this evaluation method with the following onboarding result instead of presenting disconnected claims.
Clarify whether the reduction from 9 days to 4 was measured against a pre-redesign baseline or a control group.
Explain whether the 2,300 merchants were in a pilot, an experiment, or the full rollout.
Verify that onboarding truly had a single verification step.
items.because: Other onboarding requirements may have remained unchanged.

items.says: The bullet presents a lower reported late-delivery rate as an operational improvement even though only the calculation changed.
items.because: Excluding weather-delayed shipments does not show that delivery reliability improved.

items.says: Clarify the period over which pick errors fell by 30%.
State whether the reduction applied equally at both sites or to their combined total.
The verb tense is inconsistent between “coordinated” and “prepares.”
items.because: The tense should be consistent with the completed role dates.

items.says: Add the business result of the forecast pack or S&OP review.
items.because: The bullet currently describes recurring responsibilities without a result.

items.says: Clarify your specific ownership of the S&OP process.
items.because: The bullet lists the meeting process alone.

items.says: Clarify whether the 1,800 annual driver hours are measured savings or a projected estimate.
State the period or baseline used to calculate the driver-hour savings.
Add the most relevant outcome for route completion, fuel use, overtime, or delivery performance if available.
Clarify whether the 9 tonnes were measured, estimated, or reported by the dining halls.
Make “in its first year” consistent with the project dates.
items.because: That timeframe may not align with an ongoing project.

items.says: Distinguish whether 3,100 students represents availability or actual users.
items.because: The wording does not distinguish reach from adoption.

items.says: Add an adoption, retention, transaction, or completion rate if available.
items.because: That would make the launch evidence more meaningful.

items.says: Clarify whether weekly active users increased directly after the reminder launch or over the entire term.
Explain whether user growth was measured against a control group, a prior term, or a before-and-after comparison.
Do not imply that the interviews prove reminders caused the user growth.
items.because: The interviews generated the product decision but did not establish causality.

items.says: Avoid repeating “launched” across adjacent bullets unless each launch is a distinct product milestone.
Clarify whether the 95% fill rate is an average, minimum, or peak.
Explain how staff cover shifts fell from 10 to 2.
State the period over which staff cover shifts fell.
Clarify whether the shift reduction came from the volunteer system alone or from other staffing changes.
Add what the weekly sessions produced, such as an agreed process change, implementation plan, scheduling redesign, or operational decision.
items.because: The bullet is activity-focused and lacks an outcome.

items.says: Explain your role as team lead beyond facilitating meetings.
Add measurable changes in access, wait times, workload, or utilization if available.
items.because: Those outcomes are more valuable than meeting frequency.

items.says: Rewrite the passive construction to show what you personally did.
items.because: The current wording hides your ownership.

items.says: Quantify the form reduction through fields, completion time, abandonment, or processing time.
Clarify how widely the new process was adopted and whether adoption produced a measurable result.
The merchant-onboarding claim does not belong under a hospital-network project.
items.because: Merchants do not match the project context and make the bullet look copied into the wrong section.

items.says: The bullet duplicates the Harbor Payments onboarding accomplishment.
items.because: The accomplishment should appear only under Harbor Payments.

items.says: “Roadmapping” and “requirements writing” are broad skills.
List the most valuable specific research, analytics, experimentation, or product-development methods instead of a generic inventory.
Indicate the level of Excel proficiency if appropriate.
items.because: This is especially useful if Excel supported advanced analysis, modeling, or dashboards.

items.says: Add other tools actually used in the bullets, such as SQL, survey, prototyping, or documentation tools.
Demonstrate how Jira and Amplitude were used rather than only listing them.
Consider placing Experience before Education for product-role applications.
items.because: The Experience section contains stronger professional evidence.
